function.mechanism: Hydrocolloid that hydrates to increase viscosity and form gel-structure networks, improving texture and suspension stability in foods.
common_food_categories: foods for special medical purposes (including infant-focused formulations)

adi.basis: EFSA 2018 concluded no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at refined reported uses/use levels.

efsa.key_finding: No concern for genotoxicity/carcinogenicity; no numerical ADI required; no safety concern at refined exposure (including high-end toddler exposure estimate of 72.4 mg/kg bw/day).

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED; 2025 entry indicates specifications-only update.

concerns.summary: JECFA historical note indicates potential laxative effect at high intakes.
EFSA recommended specification tightening (viable source cells and residual microbial-related constituents), indicating quality-control relevance.
Recent animal work reports microbiome modulation; current findings are not a confirmed harm signal for food-additive exposure but indicate biologic activity in gut-liver pathways.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation reports no need for numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels
EFSA abstract reports no concern for carcinogenicity and genotoxicity
Human intake studies summarized by EFSA/PubMed report no adverse effects at tested oral intakes

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI is set by EFSA/JECFA, so standard ADI exceedance assessment is not directly applicable.

risk_assessment.rationale: Authoritative reviews (EFSA/JECFA) support safety at reported uses with non-numeric ADI outcomes, while remaining concerns are mainly high-intake GI effects and specification-control details rather than severe systemic toxicity.
key_factors: EFSA 2018: no numerical ADI and no safety concern at refined exposure
JECFA: ADI not specified, latest (2025) specifications-only update
US CFR: approved direct food additive under 21 CFR 172.665
No IARC monograph classification entry located
High-intake laxative effect caveat in JECFA historical evaluation
